Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Nexus Security Inc. Q4 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for those wishing to ask a question will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Nexus Security's results for the fourth quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Nexus Security had an exceptional Q4, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection, Nexus AI Sentinel, is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers, with many achieving over 60% improvements in mean time to remediate.

Our strategy is centered around five core pillars: delivering outstanding performance in key product lines like cloud security and SASE; maintaining a robust net dollar retention rate that reflects our sticky platform; accelerating platform adoption over fragmented point products; expanding our base of high-value customers with over $100K in ARR; and proactively addressing the evolving threat landscape through relentless innovation.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we had a remarkable Q4. Revenue reached $355 million, reflecting a 28% year-over-year increase, with annualized recurring revenue hitting $1.42 billion. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $231 million, and net income was $92 million, translating to $0.72 diluted earnings per share. We are increasing our guidance for FY25 to $1.6 billion in revenue, based on these outstanding results and our robust pipeline.

Let me dive deeper into the performance of our core product lines, starting with cloud security and SASE, which together represented 62% of our total Q4 revenue and powered the bulk of that 28% ARR growth. These areas are outpacing the broader cybersecurity market's projected 13.5% CAGR through 2027 according to IDC, thanks to rapid multi-cloud shifts, ongoing hybrid workforces, and the rise of AI-driven threats.

Our cloud security portfolio—including the CNAPP solution, Nexus Guard for workload protection, and CSPM modules—generated $285 million in Q4 revenue, up 47% year-over-year and 18% sequentially. For the full year, it reached $1.05 billion, a 42% increase, now making up 37% of our total business. This was propelled by enterprises running an average of 3.2 cloud providers, as per Gartner, heightening risks from misconfigurations and lateral movement. Our agentless scanning and auto-remediation features gained strong traction, delivering net retention above 125% through 40% upsell expansion in existing accounts.

Technically, the Q3 launch of Nexus AI Sentinel, our generative AI anomaly detection engine integrated with AWS Bedrock and Azure OpenAI, enables real-time threat hunting across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS. Early users, including two Fortune 50 banks, reported 65% faster MTTR for issues like container escapes and IAM over-privileging. We also enhanced ties with Snowflake and Databricks to protect critical data from ransomware exfiltration.

Geographically, North America holds 58% of cloud security revenue, while EMEA jumped 62% year-over-year to a $210 million run rate, driven by GDPR, CCPA, and the EU's NIS2 Directive. APAC, at 22% of the segment, grew 55% following our Tokyo data center launch and alliances with hyperscalers like Alibaba Cloud. We're positioning Nexus Cloud Security to challenge leaders like Prisma with better multi-cloud support and 30% lower TCO through consumption-based pricing. We anticipate over 50% growth in FY25, backed by $450 million in remaining performance obligations from new wins, such as a large U.S. healthcare group.

Shifting to SASE, our Zero Trust Exchange—which combines SD-WAN, ZTNA, SWG, CASB, and firewall-as-a-service—posted $210 million in Q4 revenue, surging 68% year-over-year and 22% quarter-over-quarter. Full-year SASE revenue hit $780 million, up 59%, representing 28% of ARR with average contract values at $1.2 million, a 15% rise. This beats Forrester's 42% CAGR forecast for the market, amid 72% of customers maintaining permanent hybrid setups that expose VPN weaknesses.

Our Adaptive Trust Engine uses machine learning on 50 trillion daily signals for context-based access decisions, factoring in user behavior, device health, and geopolitical risks. The general availability of SASE 3.0 added DLP for SaaS and XDR integration for full visibility. This drove 15 net-new enterprise displacements of Zscaler, including a $45 million multi-year contract with a European telco where we cut their attack surface 78% via micro-segmentation.

In regions, the U.S. accounted for 52% of SASE bookings, APAC exploded 82% to $120 million run rate due to Singapore's PDPA and 5G demands, and EMEA contributed 25% with uptake in DACH amid supply chain cyber risks. With 150 global edge points of presence ensuring under 50ms latency at the 95th percentile, we outperform rivals like Cato in benchmarks. SASE boasts our highest gross margins at 88%, and we're accelerating with a $200 million acquisition of an SSE specialist to match Fortinet's FWaaS capabilities. Customer stats are stellar: 98% renewals, 135% net expansion, and six-month payback periods. For FY25, we project $1.3 billion, a 65% ramp-up in the $15 billion market.

Overall, cloud security and SASE are transforming enterprise defenses against quantum threats and regulations like SEC cyber rules, with 40% dollar-based net expansion and $620 million in cash fueling M&A and R&D for sustained 30%+ growth.

Another hallmark of our model is net dollar retention, or NDR, which captures revenue from the prior period's customer cohort, including expansions, renewals, minus churn—for our over 4,200 customers, it hit 119% in Q4, up 400 basis points sequentially from 115% and 720 basis points year-over-year from 112%. This is our 11th consecutive quarter above 110%, showing deepening reliance on our platform amid rising threats.

Our customers with over $1 million ARR, now 28% of total ARR versus 24% last year, delivered an even stronger 128% NDR, thanks to multi-year Zero Trust and XDR commitments. Expansion added 22 points, with 35% attachment for AI next-gen endpoint protection and cloud workload protection integrated with AWS Graviton and Azure Arc. Post-Change Healthcare ransomware, SASE bundling rose 42% quarter-over-quarter, with deals averaging $450,000 ARR up from $380,000.

Dollar churn stayed low at 3.2%, below peers' 7-8%, supported by 98% gross renewals on multi-year deals. Contractions at 2.1% were countered by customer success teams using our Sentinel ML for churn prediction. North America, 62% of ARR, posted 122% NDR amid ransomware surges in finance and healthcare; EMEA 116% with DLP adds against APT28 phishing; APAC 112% up sharply via Alibaba and Tencent partnerships against Lazarus Group; and LatAm 108% boosted by our Bogota data center.

This exceeds the 110% peer average by 2.5 times per Bessemer reports, as our unified EDR, NDR, and deception tech shortens land-and-expand to nine months, with 65% self-service via ServiceNow and Splunk. We expect 118-122% NDR in FY25, aided by quantum-resistant encryption pilots and GenAI red-teaming ahead of NIST standards, cementing our moat in a $225 billion market by 2028 per Gartner.

Shifting to platform adoption versus point products, we're leading the move from siloed tools—like standalone EDR or basic firewalls—to our Nexus One unified platform. Q4 platform deals made up 68% of net new ARR, up from 52% in Q4 2022 and 240 basis points from Q3, our sixth straight quarter of gains. Point products fell to 22% of net new ARR, down from 38% year-over-year, now under 18% of total ARR.

Customers average 8.2 modules per platform account, up 22% from 6.7, with 85% attach rates—beating Palo Alto's roughly seven modules and Zscaler's networking focus. Platform NRR is 128%, versus 92% for point-only. North America at 72% platform mix in new bookings, with 15 deals over $5 million ACV post-SolarWinds; EMEA 64%, up 18 points on NIS2 and EDR-XDR wins; APAC 53% accelerating to 60% by FY25 via localized AI.

Our SecureNet Cortex AI engine cuts MTTR 40% versus points, topping MITRE scores against Elastic and SentinelOne. Highlights include XDR unification reducing alert fatigue 65%, GenAI zero-trust auto-remediating 72% identity threats, and SASE 2.0 with 99.999% uptime. Customers save 42% TCO over three years per Forrester, with platform churn under 2% and 30% higher wallet share. Gartner sees platforms at $75 billion by 2027; we added 1,200 net new platform customers last year, pipeline 4.2x for H1.

On high-value customers with over $100K ARR, we closed Q4 with 520, up 16% quarter-over-quarter from 448 and 38% year-over-year from 377. They drive 68% of total ARR, up from 64%, at $465K average, plus 12%. New logos totaled 45, including three Fortune 500 financials adopting XDR with Splunk and CrowdStrike integrations, plus healthcare amid SolarWinds echoes. Expansions numbered 27, with 128% cohort NRR; 12 scaled from next-gen firewalls to zero-trust access against insiders.

North America (374 customers, 72%) grew 14% on CMMC 2.0; EMEA (99, 19%) 22% on DORA and OT security; APAC (47, 9%) doubled via Sydney center against APT41. This fuels consolidation versus point M&A fatigue, with autonomous SOC GA boosting to 600 customers by year-end and $1.2 billion ARR guide up 45%. Breaches cost $4.5 million on average per IBM.

Finally, the threat landscape is mutating under geopolitics, AI, and expanding surfaces—our platform processes 500 billion daily events from 15,000 customers. Incidents rose 37% year-over-year, breaching 2.8 billion records in H1 alone. Ransomware at 42% of mitigations demands $4.7 million but payouts fell to 28% thanks to our shield auto-isolating in 90 seconds for 85% cases. AI phishing with deepfakes up 150%, polymorphic malware 1.2 million quarterly, supply chains +55%, nation-states 19%, cloud misconfigs 72%, OT exploits +61%, quantum emerging.

North America +35% ARR with $150 million hyperscaler deal; EMEA 29% on NIS2 fines; APAC 42% countering APT41 DDoS. Our $450 million R&D targets GenAI at 99.2% accuracy, zero-trust orchestration, sovereign AI—driving 98% retention, 22% upsells, $3.5 billion pipeline.

Next, Taylor will provide more technical details.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape, including Nexus AI Sentinel for cloud anomalies, Adaptive Trust for SASE context, and Cortex for platform-wide orchestration. Key areas include full XDR unification, zero-trust automation, and post-quantum kits, validated by MITRE and AV-TEST leadership.

Morgan Patel: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, from GDPR/NIS2 telemetry to SEC disclosures and sovereign data handling.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press star then one if you have a question. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen: Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Jordan, on cloud security and SASE, those growth rates are impressive—can you talk more about sustainability into FY25, especially with the tuck-in acquisition and competitive positioning?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Mike. Absolutely, sustainability is baked in. The $450 million RPO and $1.3 billion SASE guide reflect multi-year commitments. Our 30% TCO edge and multi-cloud superiority are winning share, as seen in Zscaler displacements and healthcare logos. The SSE acquisition accelerates FWaaS parity, targeting 30%+ growth with $620 million cash runway.

Operator: Next question from Lisa Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Patel: Great, thanks. Jordan, your NDR at 119% with low churn is standout—how much is driven by regions like APAC, and any risks to the 118-122% band?

Jordan Lee: Lisa, thanks. APAC's 112% acceleration from hyperscaler ties and Lazarus counters is key, alongside NA's 122% in ransomware-hit sectors. Churn risks are minimal at 3.2% dollar basis, offset by ML predictions. Platformization and self-serve expansions keep us above peers, with quantum pilots fortifying FY25.

Operator: Next from David Ruiz with JPMorgan.

David Ruiz: Hi, team. Taylor, platform adoption at 68%—how are innovations like Cortex contributing, and what's the module depth trajectory?

Taylor Kim: David, excellent question. Cortex's 40% MTTR improvement and 65% alert reduction drive 8.2 modules average, heading to 10. MITRE-validated XDR/SSE convergence and GenAI policies yield 128% NRR, outpacing points amid Gartner tailwinds.

Operator: Final question from Emma Walsh with Barclays.

Emma Walsh: Thanks. Alex, with 520 high-value customers and threat surges, thoughts on cohort growth and pipeline conversion?

Alex Rivera: Emma, spot on. The 38% YoY jump to 520, at 68% ARR share, stems from F500 wins and 128% expansions. Threats like AI phishing and OT exploits boost urgency—our $3.5 billion pipeline at 4.2x visibility positions us for 600 by year-end, executing our five pillars for long-term value.

Alex Rivera: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
